summary: Webhook deliveries that fail are now retried up to five times with exponential backoff, inside the worker that picked the event up. A new attempts column records how many tries each event used, and the last_status column is dropped.

claims.text: Failed deliveries retry up to 5 times with exponential backoff.
claims.evidence: Ran deliver() against a stub that returns 503 four times, then 200. Measured waits of 1.1 s, 2.3 s, 4.2 s and 8.9 s. The fifth attempt was delivered.

claims.text: Nothing changes for a delivery that succeeds first time.
claims.evidence: Replayed 200 recorded deliveries on base and head. The outgoing requests are byte-identical. The only database difference is attempts = 1 on head.

claims.text: Receivers will not see duplicate events.
claims.evidence: A stub endpoint that answers after 6 s, and does process the request, received the same event 5 times. No header distinguishes the attempts.

claims.text: The migration is safe to run with no downtime.
claims.evidence: The new column is NOT NULL with no default, and last_status is dropped in the same migration. Whether that is safe depends on whether old workers run during the migration, which is not visible from this repository.

claims.text: A worker now holds its slot for up to 40 s per event while it retries.
claims.evidence: The backoff sleeps inside deliver(), and pool.ts awaits deliver() before claiming the next event. The description does not mention worker capacity.

decisions.title: A delivery that times out is sent again, so a slow endpoint receives the same event up to five times.
decisions.detail: On base, a timeout marked the event failed and stopped. On head, a timeout counts as retryable. The endpoint may have processed the first request; nothing in the later requests tells it they are the same event apart from X-Webhook-Id, which receivers are not told to dedupe on.
decisions.question: Are duplicate deliveries acceptable here?

options.label: Not acceptable
options.detail: Retries must carry an idempotency key before this merges.
options.comment: A timeout is retried, but the endpoint may already have processed the first attempt. Please send an `Idempotency-Key` derived from `event.id` on every attempt, and document that receivers should dedupe on it. With the current code an endpoint that answers in 6 s receives the same event 5 times.

options.label: Acceptable
options.detail: At-least-once delivery is the contract. The description should say so.
options.comment: Accepting at-least-once delivery. Please correct the description: it says receivers will not see duplicates, and on a timeout they will.

options.label: I do not know
options.detail: Ask the author, and keep this open.
options.comment: Is at-least-once delivery intended? On a timeout the same event can reach an endpoint up to 5 times, with no key to dedupe on. Probe attached.

decisions.title: The migration adds a NOT NULL column with no default and drops a column the old code still writes.
decisions.detail: Until every worker runs the new code, an old worker's INSERT omits attempts and its UPDATE writes last_status. Both fail once the migration has run. Running the migration after the deploy fails the other way: new code writes attempts before it exists.
decisions.question: How does this repository deploy: can old and new code run against the same database?

options.label: They overlap
options.detail: Rolling deploys. The migration must be split.
options.comment: Workers roll, so old and new code run against the same schema for a while. Please split this: (1) add `attempts integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` now, (2) drop `last_status` in a later migration once no running code writes it.

options.label: I do not know
options.detail: Ask the author to state the deploy order.
options.comment: Do old workers keep running while 0142 migrates? If they do, the NOT NULL column needs a default and dropping `last_status` has to wait for a later migration.

decisions.title: A worker holds its slot for up to 40 s while it retries one event.
decisions.detail: pool.ts runs 8 workers and each awaits deliver() before claiming the next event. With retries inside deliver(), one dead endpoint occupies a slot for 40 s instead of 5 s. Eight dead endpoints stall all delivery for 40 s.
decisions.question: Is that capacity cost acceptable for now?

options.label: No
options.detail: Retries should be scheduled as separate jobs.
options.comment: Sleeping inside `deliver()` holds one of 8 worker slots for up to 40 s per failing event. Please schedule each retry as a delayed job (set `next_attempt_at` and release the slot) so one bad endpoint cannot starve the pool.

options.label: Yes, with a follow-up
options.detail: Fine at current volume. Note it and move on.
options.comment: Not blocking: retries sleep inside the worker, which holds a slot for up to 40 s per failing event. Worth a follow-up to move retries to delayed jobs before volume grows.

options.label: I do not know
options.detail: Ask what volume and failure rate to expect.
options.comment: What failure rate do we expect? With retries inside `deliver()`, each failing event holds one of 8 worker slots for up to 40 s.

context.lede: You last reviewed src/delivery five months ago and have not read src/worker. This covers what the change leans on and skips what you know from ledger's outbox.

path.label: deliver()
path.note: was send(): one POST, 5 s timeout

facts.text: A worker handles one event at a time and awaits deliver() before claiming the next, so anything slow inside deliver() takes one of only 8 slots.
A claimed row has a 60 s lease. If a worker is still busy when it ends, another worker can claim the same row.
The only identifier sent to the endpoint is X-Webhook-Id. The public docs do not tell receivers to dedupe on it.

analogy.text: This does the same job as the outbox retry you reviewed in acme/ledger. The difference: ledger sets next_attempt_at and frees the worker between tries; this sleeps inside the worker.

ruleHits.note: Retries of a POST carry no idempotency key. Probe fails.
attempts is NOT NULL with no default, and no deploy order is stated.
The two new exported functions in backoff.ts: backoff has a doc comment; sleep does not, but is one line.
